NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A young navigator notices an odd swell and wants to change course: trust them, or keep the planned route.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The canoe is two days out on its way to the fishing islands. (friend), on (friend.his/her) first long voyage, has noticed a swell coming from the wrong direction and says something is out there, an island or a reef, that is not on the route. (subject), who has made this trip thirty times, has never seen it. Should they change course?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: They change course. By dawn, a reef appears out of nowhere, exactly where the swell was bending. Beyond it is a lagoon so full of fish the crew laughs out loud. (subject) is silent for a long time, then shakes (friend)'s hand.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: They keep the route. It is a quiet voyage. (friend) keeps watching the swell, and draws it on a piece of bark. Years later, when (friend.he/she) has a canoe of (friend.his/her) own, (friend.he/she) goes looking. (subject) insists on coming.
